thinking_and_logic: Your final approach maintains a hash map from value to its index as you scan left-to-right. At each position i with value n, you compute complement = target - n and check if it has appeared earlier; if so, you immediately return the earlier index and i. Checking before inserting ensures you don’t reuse the same element, and storing indices allows correct output even with duplicates like [3,3].
code_assessment: The final code matches the canonical optimal solution from the answer key: single pass + hash map of seen values to indices, checking the complement before inserting the current value. This achieves O(n) time versus the brute-force O(n^2) start, while remaining robust to duplicates and preserving original indices (unlike sort-based approaches). The implementation is minimal and correct given the constraints and the “exactly one answer” guarantee.
